sections.h2: Where is Butler County, Ohio, and which communities does it include?
sections.html:
Butler County lies in southwestern Ohio, with Hamilton County to its south, Montgomery County to the northeast and Indiana to the west. Hamilton is the seat and the largest city. Wikipedia gives 470 square miles of area, mostly the valleys of the Great Miami and Little Miami rivers. It was formed in 1803 from part of Hamilton County and is named for General Richard Butler.

Seven cities sit inside the county: Fairfield, Hamilton, Middletown, Monroe, Oxford, Sharonville and Trenton. Five villages and thirteen civil townships fill in the rest, among them West Chester, Liberty, Lemon and Reily. Miami University was chartered in 1809 on a township the legislature set aside for a college. Sixteen school districts have territory here, including Lakota, Fairfield, Hamilton, Middletown and Talawanda.

The 2020 census counted 390,357 residents, which ranks Butler seventh among Ohio counties. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 400,128. A property tax bill in this county therefore depends heavily on which of the many taxing districts a house falls into.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Butler County homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau QuickFacts table for Butler County shows a larger and pricier market than its eastern Ohio neighbors. The 2020 to 2024 figures are:

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing: $258,500.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 69.9 percent among 146,822 households.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,665. Without a mortgage: $619.
  • Median gross rent: $1,135.
  • Median household income: $81,590.
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,021, against 158,143 housing units.

Population grew 2.5 percent between the April 2020 base and July 2025.

sections.h2: How much did the 2026 reappraisal raise Butler County values?
sections.html:
The auditor reports a median residential and agricultural increase of 19 percent for tax year 2026, payable in 2027, and a median 20 percent for commercial and industrial property. The state Department of Tax Equalization approved the value abstract on June 25. The office adds that its sales ratio sits near 90 percent of full market value.

Source: Butler County Auditor news release, which lists every jurisdiction.

The release stresses that voted levies move a bill more than value does. It names a new countywide 2-mill developmental disabilities levy at about $70 per $100,000 of value, and a 4.49-mill Fairfield Township fire levy at about $157 per $100,000. Those are the office's own figures. The release says new state laws blunt the effect of higher values, and the auditor's homepage points to an inflation cap credit on second-half bills under House Bill 186.

Ohio's cycle brings a reappraisal every six years and a triennial update halfway between. Butler County's schedule lists 2026 as the latest reappraisal and 2032 as the next, with updates in 2023 and 2029.

sections.h2: How is a Butler County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The treasurer explains that taxable value is 35 percent of the auditor's fair market value. The auditor multiplies that taxable value by the total mill rate and divides by 1,000. Levies and special assessments are added, then reduction credits come off.

  • Parcel numbers. A real estate parcel is a letter followed by 13 numbers, and about 160,000 parcels exist in the county.
  • Taxing districts. The treasurer counts 66 separate districts, so a house in Hamilton and one in Liberty Township can carry different rates.
  • Reduction factors. A levy cannot raise more than it did when voters passed it, so the state applies a reduction factor to the gross rate.
  • Credits. The non-business credit and the owner-occupancy credit apply only to levies in place before the November 2013 election. Homestead is a separate reduction for qualifying seniors, disabled owners and veterans.

Special assessments for items like street paving or weed removal also show on the bill and go back to the government that levied them.

sections.h2: When are Butler County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The treasurer collects twice a year. The first half is typically due in mid to late February and the second half in early August, and the printed bill carries the exact date. The 2025 second half was mailed on July 20, 2026, and was due Wednesday, August 19, 2026. The treasurer's number for a missing bill is (513) 887-3181.

Ohio collects a year in arrears, so a bill paid in 2026 covers tax year 2025. A payment more than ten days late draws a 10 percent penalty. Paid in full within the first ten days, the penalty is 5 percent, as the treasurer's timeline explains under section 323.121.

Interest is added twice a year. On prior-year balances it begins on the first day of the month after the second-half due date, and on December 1 interest is added to the total unpaid balance. An owner can file an Application for Remission of Penalty, but the law allows remission only in limited cases.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a value in Butler County?
sections.html:
A complaint goes to the Board of Revision, which consists of the county auditor, the county treasurer and a member of the board of county commissioners. The auditor says the board reviews values, not the amount of tax owed. The filing window is January 1 to March 31, and an owner generally files once in each three-year valuation period.

Filing steps, as the office describes them:

  • Complete DTE Form 1, Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property, with any supporting documentation.
  • Submit it through the office's online vendor, by email to bor@bcohio.gov, or by mail.
  • Expect a Notice of Hearing by email or certified mail.
  • Allow three to four weeks after the hearing for the Notice of Result.

A request to cut market value by $50,000 or more can draw a counter-complaint from another eligible party such as a school board. The decision can be appealed within 30 days of mailing to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the Common Pleas Court, with notice to the board as well. The 2026 values open for complaint in January and close March 31 of the following year.

sections.h2: What do Butler County sellers pay at the auditor and recorder?
sections.html:
The deed visits the auditor first and the recorder second. The auditor's FAQ prints a conveyance fee of $3.00 per thousand of the sale price, rounded up to the next hundred, plus $.50 per parcel, with a real estate minimum of $3.00 plus the parcel fee. Payment is by cash or check made out to the Butler County Auditor.

DTE Form 100 goes with an ordinary sale and Form 100EX with an exempt transfer. The legal description must be attached, and the auditor asks owners to have the Engineer's Office at 513-867-5744 preapprove it before submitting. Transfers can come by mail, in person or by e-file.

The recorder's fee sheet, effective January 1, 2025, lists the following:

  • $39.00 for a deed, mortgage or lease up to two pages, including a $5.00 preservation surcharge, and $8.00 per added page.
  • $20.00 more for a document that misses the standard layout rules.
  • $4.00 per reference for a satisfaction or release.
  • $2.00 per page for copies and $1.00 per document to certify.

The sheet asks for parcel numbers on every deed, a self-addressed stamped envelope, and a prepared-by statement on documents notarized in Ohio. Turnaround is listed as 24 hours. The recorder's office is at 130 High Street in Hamilton, and the fee sheet gives (513) 887-3192.

faqs.q: When is the second-half Butler County tax bill due?
faqs.a: It is usually due in early August. The 2025 second-half bill was due Wednesday, August 19, 2026, after mailing on July 20. The first half is typically due in mid to late February, so read the date on the bill.

faqs.q: How did Butler County values change in 2026?
faqs.a: Residential and agricultural values rose by a median of 19 percent, and commercial and industrial by 20 percent. Changes differ by place, from a median 39 percent in Lemon Township to 12 percent in the city of Fairfield. New voted levies affect the bill as much as value does.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Butler County valuation every year?
faqs.a: Generally no. An owner may file once in each three-year valuation period, with some exceptions the statute lists. The window runs from January 1 to March 31, and the form is DTE Form 1 filed with the auditor as secretary of the Board of Revision.

faqs.q: What is the conveyance fee when a Butler County house sells?
faqs.a: The auditor prints $3.00 per thousand of the sale price, rounded up to the next hundred, plus $.50 per parcel. Checks go to the Butler County Auditor. Ask the auditor at 513-887-3154 about exemptions that call for Form 100EX.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Butler County?
faqs.a: The recorder's 2025 fee sheet lists $39.00 for up to two pages, which includes a $5.00 preservation surcharge, and $8.00 for each extra page. A document that fails the layout standard adds $20.00. Call (513) 887-3192 with questions.
